newsitem.title: CANADA: Uniglobe offers stock in new online travel service.
newsitem.headline: Uniglobe offers stock in new online travel service.

text.p: Travel-agency franchisor Uniglobe Travel International spun off part of a new Internet travel service on Tuesday in a public stock offering.
Uniglobe, which says it is the world's biggest franchisor of travel agencies with 1,140 outlets in 16 countries, sold about 25 percent of Uniglobe Travel Online Inc to investors.

Uniglobe said it was the first travel company to offer investors a stake in its online service. The offering raised $2.5 million Canadian ($1.85 million) with the issue of 1.25 million shares at C$2 ($1.48) each.
The shares began trading Tuesday on the Vancouver Stock Exchange at $C4, twice the offering price, and ended the day at C$5.35 on turnover of 350,000 shares.
The public offering coincided with the company's first efforts to publicize the online service which it has been testing since June.
The service offers travel packages, flight, rail and hotel prices, reservations, discounted trips and travel information.
"The timing is perfect (for the launch). The market is very interested," Uniglobe chairman Gary Charlwood said.
Uniglobe is part of Charlwood's privately held business empire that includes Century 21 Real Estate Canada Ltd.
"We believe there will be lot of commerce exercised on the Internet," he said, citing one industry forecast that electronic commerce will hit $150 billion a year by 2000.
Uniglobe's online service is likely to face stiff competition.

For example, travel agency Carlson Wagonlit Travel has an Internet offering. Microsoft Corp and American Express Co. also announced plans in July to offer a corporate travel booking service using Internet standards that would be available in the first half of 1997.
Uniglobe said its Internet service will stand out because of consumer recognition of the Uniglobe name and support for users from its 6,000 travel agents.
